title: Hip Fracture
lead: One of the most important fractures in older adults: early mobilisation saves function and lives.
case: An 82-year-old woman had a hemiarthroplasty yesterday for a displaced femoral neck fracture after tripping on a rug. She lived alone and walked with a stick. BP 118/70 lying, 96/60 sitting with dizziness. Hb slightly low.
> Plan: return to lying, inform the medical team about the orthostatic drop, bed exercises and breathing exercises, retry sitting later after fluids or review.
plan: return to lying, inform the medical team about the orthostatic drop, bed exercises and breathing exercises, retry sitting later after fluids or review.
qa: Why mobilise on day 1? To reduce complications and improve recovery of walking.
What does her blood pressure drop mean? Orthostatic hypotension, possibly from anaemia or fluid loss. Do not push standing; inform the team.
What is the long-term exercise priority? Progressive strength and balance training plus falls prevention.
What else must be addressed before discharge? Home hazards (rugs), aids, support, and bone health.
Sudden breathlessness during walking? Treat as possible pulmonary embolism: emergency.

redFlags.Finding: Sudden breathlessness, chest pain, tachycardia, low SpO2
redFlags.Immediate action: Stop; lie the patient back; call medical emergency team

redFlags.Finding: Systolic BP drop with dizziness or loss of consciousness
redFlags.Immediate action: Return to bed, elevate legs, inform team

redFlags.Finding: Leg shortening and rotation after movement
redFlags.Immediate action: Do not move the leg; medical team

manualNotes: Not a priority. Gentle soft-tissue work or assisted range only for comfort.

exercise.Exercise: Ankle pumps, static quadriceps and gluteal sets, deep breathing
Sit-to-stand from a raised chair, standing hip abduction and extension at the frame, mini-squats, walking with frame
Progress to stick, step-ups, stairs practice, heel raises
Progressive resistance training for hip extensors, abductors and quadriceps, balance training (Otago-style program), walking
exercise.Dose: 2 to 3 times a week for months [Ref – to verify]

exerciseNotes: Hip precautions after hemiarthroplasty or replacement depend on surgical approach and local protocol. Many modern pathways use minimal precautions; follow the surgeon's instructions exactly.
modalityNotes: Ice for swelling and pain; not essential. Compression stockings and anticoagulation are medical decisions.
pathway: Pre-operative: chest care, positioning, explain the plan.
Day 0 to 1: mobilise out of bed.
Ward: daily walking, transfers, ADL with occupational therapy.
Discharge: aids, home safety, exercise program.
Community: strength and balance training, falls prevention, bone health medication through the doctor.
